title: perf-bench-scratch-kvcache-batching
content:
Notes / scratchpad for short latency/throughput runs exploring KV-cache + batching behavior

Context:
- small personal bench to triage odd p95 spikes we saw on dedicated pools last week. trying to reproduce with isolated runner.
- hardware: single A100-SXM (80GB) on dev-dedicated-1; also did quick run on 2x A10 for low-memory configs.
- runtime: staging build from PR 238 (kernel selection + batch coalescing changes)
- model variants: 13B flax-open weights (fp16), int8 quantized with q4f16-ish pipeline, and a micro-quantized 7B to sanity-check.
- workload: chat-style prefix (avg prompt tokens 120), generation target 256 tokens, 8 concurrent clients driving traffic, synthetic arrival with poisson inter-arrival.

Test matrix (high-level):
- KV-cache enabled vs disabled
- batching target sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16
- quantization: fp16 vs int8
- concurrency sweep: 1, 4, 8, 16

Quick results summary (raw observations):
- baseline (fp16, KV off, batch=1): throughput 6.2 req/s, p50 160ms, p95 520ms
- KV on (fp16, batch=1): throughput 7.1 req/s, p50 140ms, p95 480ms (small win from prefix cache on repeated tokens)
- batch=8 (fp16, KV on): throughput 28 req/s, p50 340ms, p95 950ms (higher throughput but p95 suffers due to packing delays + tail queueing)
- batch=8 + int8 quant: throughput 36 req/s, p50 260ms, p95 730ms (int8 reduces per-token time significantly; p95 improved over fp16)
- aggressive batching (16) caused occasional OOM on int8 path for 13B variant on A100 (need to cap seq len or use kv prefetch)
- concurrency effect: at concurrency >=8 we start to see queuing-induced p95 spikes even when target batch size kept small; microbursts amplify tail latency

Mini table (representative numbers):
- model: 13B fp16, KV on
  - batch=1: qps 7.1, p50 140ms, p95 480ms
  - batch=4: qps 18.5, p50 220ms, p95 640ms
  - batch=8: qps 28.0, p50 340ms, p95 950ms

- model: 13B int8, KV on
  - batch=1: qps 9.8, p50 120ms, p95 420ms
  - batch=8: qps 36.0, p50 260ms, p95 730ms

Observed patterns / hypotheses:
- KV-cache helps steady-state throughput and lowers medians when prompts share prefixes, but doesn't eliminate tail spikes caused by batching waits + scheduling jitter.
- int8 quant path gives solid per-token speedups but increases memory pressure at larger batch sizes (surprising, likely due to different allocator behavior + kernel workspace for some int8 fused ops).
- larger batch sizes improve aggregate throughput but amplify p95 due to head-of-line blocking and scheduling latency for the first request in a batch. This is consistent with continuous batching model trade-offs.
- concurrency-driven microbursts: the scheduler coalesces small bursts into larger batches which sometimes exceed safe memory for quantized kernels; need better admission control or soft caps per model variant.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- reproduce with stricter sequence-length control: ensure generation length capped at 128 and re-run batch=16 int8 to confirm OOM reproducibility.
- add per-request queuing time tracing to separate 'wait for batch' vs 'compute' in traces (tie to tracing hooks in PR 238).
- try hybrid policy: target_batch 8 but fallback to flush after 30ms to reduce p95. Measure p50/p95 trade-off.
- evaluate allocator settings: tcmalloc vs default + tune fused-kernel workspace allocations for int8 path.
- run on dedicated 2xA100 to see whether OOM behaviour persists at pool scale (maybe memory fragmentation issue per-process).
- run against a more realistic prompt set (not synthetic) to measure prefix hit rate impact on KV cache benefit.

Quick decision log:
- not ready to ship batch=16 default for 13B-int8. need mitigations (flush timeout, memory caps).
- enable KV-cache by default for chat routes with high prefix reuse; but attach a per-route p95 SLO and fallback policy.

Experiment artifacts / commands used:
- bench runner: scripts/bench/kv_batch_runner.py (local branch samira/kv-bench)
- perf capture: perf/trace-2026-02-20-a100-flash.tar.gz (attached to PR 238 comment)
- quick reproducer: locust script at tests/load/locust-kv-batch.py

Links / refs:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/238 (kernel selection + batch coalescing)
- Jira: JIRA-INF-342 (investigate p95 spikes on dedicated pools)
- Confluence draft: confluence:perf-kvcache-bench (working doc)

Next steps (short):
1) add 'flush after 30ms' policy to bench runner and measure p95 impact (Samira)
2) instrument 'wait-for-batch' in tracing and re-run heavy concurrency sweep (Jordan)
3) try int8 allocator tweak and re-run batch=8/16 on A100 (Alex)

Random notes / scratch ideas:
- maybe try tiny per-client jittering to reduce synchronous microbursts from downstream clients (simulate real clients)
- consider per-model batch caps exposed in route config (so enterprise customers can tune per SLO)

End of scratchpad.
_note: personal/scratchpad log; not a polished report
